clauses.reason: Section 1 directs the Director of the Office of Personnel Management to make arrangements for voluntary agencies to solicit federal employees through an annual Combined Federal Campaign. Executive Order 12404 (signed 1983-02-10) deleted section 1 and inserted a replacement section (strike-and-insert; before: national voluntary health and welfare agencies and other national voluntary agencies; after: voluntary health and welfare agencies), and Executive Order 13743 (signed 2016-10-13) revised section 1 again into subsections (a) and (b) naming voluntary health and welfare organizations and adding volunteer-time pledges and annuitant contributions. The clause continues, amended, under the owner ruling on strike-and-insert amendments; the substance of section 1 was rewritten, which a human reviewer should note. The current text appears in the extracted 5 U.S.C. 1101 note (not cited).

research_rationale:
Executive Order 12353 of 1982-03-23 (47 FR 12785) set up the Combined Federal Campaign under the Director of the Office of Personnel Management. The held official text was read in full; its first inventory omitted sections 8 and 9, which follow the page break, so the inventory is corrected to nine sections with section 9 split into a performed revocation and a continuing savings sentence. Executive Orders 12404 and 13743 amended it and were read in full; neither ends it. The extracted U.S. Code note to 5 U.S.C. 1101 (not cited) reproduces the order as amended, the eCFR bounded search as of 2026-10-14 returned current regulations that rely on it, and the Federal Register catalog search found no revocation. The order is therefore claimed in force on 2026-10-14. The held official text is a machine text layer (OCR) of the Federal Register page; its spans quote the OCR text.

savings.reason: Both amending orders preserved rules made under the order: Executive Order 12404 section 2 and Executive Order 13743 section 2(d) say rules, regulations and directives continued or issued under Executive Order 12353 continue in effect until revoked or modified under the amending order. These rules (OPM rules at 5 CFR part 950) are independent implementing instruments that continue while the order stays in force; the order itself has no end date and no savings of its own other than the section 9 continuation of Executive Order 10927 directives.
